drafts.walkScript: Start with swift. Swift means moving at great speed. Fast means the same, so it matches. Slow is the opposite. A cheetah and a race can be fast, but neither means fast.
Start with damp. Damp means a little wet. Moist also means a little wet, so it matches. Dry is the opposite. A towel and a puddle go with wetness, but neither means wet.
Start with hollow. Hollow means having nothing inside. Empty also means nothing inside, so it matches. Solid is the opposite. A drum and a log are things, not words that mean empty.
Start with rare. Rare means not found often. Scarce also means hard to find, so it matches. Common is the opposite. A coin and a stamp may be rare, but they are things, not meanings.
Start with obedient. Obedient means doing what you are told. Well-behaved is the closest, so it matches. Disobedient is the opposite. A dog can obey a command, but neither word means obedient.
Start with luminous. Luminous means giving off light, often a soft glow. Bright is the closest, so it matches. Dull is the opposite. The moon and a lamp give light, but they are things, not meanings.

Start with notorious. Notorious means well known for something bad. Infamous means the same, so it matches. Reputable is the opposite, as it means having a good name. A criminal or a headline may be notorious, but neither word means it.

Start with rapid. Rapid means moving at great speed. Slow is the opposite, and a race is a thing, not a speed. One option means rushing because time is short, which is a different idea. The option left means fast, so it matches.
Start with timid. Timid means nervous around others. Shy means the same, so it matches. Terrified is far too strong. Quiet is only one part of timid, while polite means something else.
Start with sturdy. Sturdy means built to be strong. Strong is the closest, so it matches. Unbreakable goes too far. Heavy or wooden things can be sturdy, but those words mean something else.
Start with feeble. Feeble means having very little strength. Frail means the same, so it matches. Helpless goes too far. Pale or elderly people can be feeble, but those words mean something else.

Start with AMIABLE in the sentence. It means friendly, warm in a kind way. Friendly is the closest, so it matches. Grumpy is the opposite. Cheerful means happy, while chatty is only one part of being friendly.

Start with EXQUISITE in the sentence. It means very beautiful, with fine detail. Beautiful is the closest, so it matches. Pretty is not strong enough, while costly means something else. Sharp fits another meaning, as in a sharp pain.
Start with BENEVOLENT in the sentence. It means caring about others, keen to do good. Kind means the same, so it matches. Saintly goes too far. Polite is about manners, while wealthy is about money.

Start with JOVIAL in the sentence. It means cheerful in a warm, friendly way. Cheerful means the same, so it matches. Ecstatic is far too strong. Silly means foolish, while loud is only one part of it.
Start with MELANCHOLY in the sentence. It means sad in a quiet, thoughtful way. Sad is the closest, so it matches. Heartbroken is far too strong. A gentle or slow tune is not always sad.
